summary: BBN's traffic statistics for the ARPANET hosts for March 1973, as tables of packets output per host. Data for two days was missing. It updates RFC 482 and was itself updated by RFC 509.

eli5.summary: A monthly scoreboard of how many messages each computer on the early network sent.

questions: how much traffic did the arpanet carry in 1973
what is a host throughput summary
subtitle: A monthly scoreboard of how many packets each ARPANET host sent in March 1973.

tldr.problem: People running and using the early network wanted to know how much traffic each host was generating.
tldr.mechanism: A BBN staff member circulated a table of packets output per host for March 1973, split into internode and intranode traffic, with totals and a daily average.
tldr.outcome: It is a data report, not a protocol. It updates RFC 482 and was itself updated by RFC 509, the April 1973 report.

today: RFC 497 is a historical record of one month of traffic. It updates RFC 482 and was updated by RFC 509, the April 1973 report.

sections.title: What the Report Is
sections.content:
RFC 497 is a short cover note, "Attached are the Host traffic statistics for the month of March 1973", followed by one table. It is dated 10 April 1973 and carries the name of A. McKenzie of BBN-NET. It is a data release and defines no protocol.

The table is headed Host Throughput Summary (Packets Output). It notes that data is missing for days 16 and 20 of the month.
sections.eli5: It is a note that says: here are the numbers for last month. The numbers are the whole point.

sections.title: How the Table Is Laid Out
sections.content:
Each site (UCLA, SRI, UCSB, BBN, MIT and so on) has one line per numbered host, for example UCLA HOST 0 and UCLA HOST 1. Columns give internode packets, intranode packets and the total.

For sites with more than one host, a subtotal line follows. It also gives the average daily internode figure and the number of days counted, which is 29 for every listed site. BELV and LBL are reported as having no traffic.
sections.eli5: Each school gets a row, and each computer in the school gets a line. Next to each line are counts of notes sent to other schools and notes kept inside the same school.

sections.title: The Network Totals
sections.content:
The bottom of the table gives network-wide figures: 56405660 internode packets and 20045130 intranode packets. The daily average is 1945023 internode and 691212 intranode, and the average per node-day is 54028 and 19200.

The last line reports a ratio of packets to messages (internode) of 1.08. The largest single internode count shown is 9401088, for ISI HOST 1, and the largest intranode count is 10893160 for the combined Harvard (HARV) hosts.
sections.eli5: At the bottom, someone added everything up and also worked out the average per day, so you can see how busy the whole network was.
